name: io.github.semcycle/actbook
description: Booking, CRM, contracts, invoicing, payments and outreach for entertainers & small businesses.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The signed-in account and what this key can do. user_type is 'full' or 'limited'; a limited user's `permissions` lists the tool areas they may use (and `access` says it in words) — anything outside them is refused with no_access.

tools.name: set_landing_page
tools.description: Set which screen ActBook opens to for the signed-in user (after login and when the installed app launches): landing_page = home | calendar | schedule | pipeline | inbox. landing_page_phone sets a different one for phones (empty = same as landing_page). whoami shows the current value under `landing`.

tools.name: business_summary
tools.description: Key numbers: upcoming gigs, gigs in the next 30 days, bookings this month, open quotes, active clients, booked value year-to-date.

tools.name: search
tools.description: PRIMARY LOOKUP — use this first whenever the user names a person, company, or place. Searches clients AND their contacts together: client/company names, contact first/last names, titles, email addresses, phone numbers, and street/city/state/zip. A name that isn't a client is very often a contact (e.g. a teacher or planner) attached to one — this finds those where a plain client search would not. Multi-word queries match all words. Pass include='notes' to search the free-text NOTES instead (per-date gig notes, booking comments and internal manager notes, your calendar notes) — e.g. to find the gig whose note mentions parking.

tools.name: list_schedule
tools.description: Gigs on the calendar between two dates (default: the next 90 days). q = free-text search across client, project, act, show, venue, city/state and the date's notes — with q and no dates it searches ALL dates, past and future. act_id = only dates played by that act (comma-separate several; 0 = dates with no act). Each gig carries its effective act_id/act_name (the date's act, else the booking's, else the show's).

tools.name: get_calendar_view
tools.description: The signed-in user's default calendar views: which view /calendar opens in on a computer (desktop) and on a phone (phone) — month, week or list.

tools.name: set_calendar_view
tools.description: Set the signed-in user's default calendar view (write scope): desktop and/or phone = month | week | list. Per user — teammates keep their own.

tools.name: get_calendar_sync
tools.description: This user's two-way calendar sync: Google (connected?, email, last sync/error — connecting Google is a browser sign-in at connect_url) and Apple iCloud (connected Apple ID, the calendar gigs are written to, which calendars count as busy, every iCloud calendar with its url, gigs synced, busy events read, last sync/error). Never returns passwords.

tools.name: connect_apple_calendar
tools.description: Connect Apple iCloud Calendar for two-way sync (write scope). Needs the Apple ID email and an APP-SPECIFIC password (not their normal Apple password): appleid.apple.com -> Sign-In and Security -> App-Specific Passwords -> generate one named "ActBook". write=new (default) puts gigs in a new "ActBook gigs" calendar; write=later connects without writing gigs until a calendar is chosen with update_apple_calendar. busy_calendars (urls) defaults to every calendar except the gigs one. Only ask the user for the password if they offer it; otherwise send them to /calendar -> Calendars.

tools.name: update_apple_calendar
tools.description: Change Apple iCloud sync choices (write scope): write = 'new' (the "ActBook gigs" calendar) | a calendar url from get_calendar_sync | '' (stop writing gigs); busy_calendars = calendar urls whose events count as busy; sync_enabled; blocks_availability (all-day iCloud events close those dates on the booking form); refresh_calendars=true re-reads the calendar list from iCloud first. Moving gigs to another calendar removes them from the old one.

tools.name: sync_apple_calendar
tools.description: Sync Apple iCloud now (write scope): push upcoming gigs into the chosen iCloud calendar and read busy times back (it also runs every 15 minutes). Returns pushed/updated/deleted/pulled/removed and any error.

tools.name: disconnect_apple_calendar
tools.description: Disconnect Apple iCloud Calendar (write scope). Gigs already in iCloud stay there; ActBook stops updating them and forgets the iCloud busy times. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Booked dates in a month, or whether a specific date is free (pass date=YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: list_bookings
tools.description: List bookings. Filter by q (text), status (all|confirmed|quotes), upcoming=true (next gig today or later) or past=true (last gig date before today), and/or a gig-date range from/to (YYYY-MM-DD; keeps bookings whose gig dates overlap it). Filters combine. Each row has first_date and last_date (its gig span).

tools.name: get_booking
tools.description: One booking with its dates, line items and payments.

tools.name: create_booking
tools.description: Create a booking (or a quote with is_quote:true — defaults to a confirmed booking). start_time/end_time accept HH:MM (24h) or plain forms like '6pm'/'6:00 PM'. participants/volunteers set the headcount (default from the package if omitted). comments PRINT on the contract (client-facing detail); manager_notes are internal and do NOT print (put provenance like 'from handwritten note' here). Several dates on one booking: pass dates=[{date, start_time, end_time, project_type_id, price, act_id}, ...] (the first is the main date; price defaults to the SUM of the dates' prices). act_id per date only applies when the account has 'Book multiple acts per booking' on (setting multi_act_booking, Agent plan); otherwise every date gets the booking's act_id.

tools.name: update_booking
tools.description: Update a booking: project, price, is_quote, comments (print on the contract), manager_notes (internal, do not print), headcount (participants/volunteers), event type (project_type_id, applied to all its dates), deposit (whole percent 0-100), contact_id (which of the client's existing contacts the contract and signing/payment emails go to), and client_id to reassign the booking to a different client.

tools.name: list_event_dates
tools.description: A booking's event dates with event type, times, location and headcount.

tools.name: update_event_date
tools.description: Edit one event date on a booking: type (the event-type / project_type_id), date, start_time, end_time, venue, address, city, state, zip, participants, volunteers.

tools.name: list_line_items
tools.description: Line items on a booking.

tools.name: add_line_item
tools.description: Add a line item to a booking (e.g. 'extra half hour', travel). The amount (price x quantity) is added to the booking total.

tools.name: remove_line_item
tools.description: Remove a booking line item (subtracts its amount from the total).

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: List / SELECT clients. This is the marketing selection engine: filter by q (name), tag (a grouping_id from the account's tags), state (2-letter), county (+ county_state), near_zip OR near_client (a client_id) with radius_miles for a geo radius, and has_email / has_phone (true to require one on file). Filters AND together. Each row has clients_id, name, city, state, zip, email, phone. Use the same filters with tag_clients, enroll_clients or make_call_list to act on the whole selection.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Create a client (optionally with a contact name/email/phone).

tools.name: tag_clients
tools.description: Apply a tag to a whole selection of clients at once. Target the set with EITHER client_ids (an explicit list) OR the same selection filters as list_clients (tag, state, county/county_state, near_zip/near_client + radius_miles, has_email, has_phone, q). Name the tag with grouping_id (existing tag) or tag_name (created if new — e.g. 'Marked for mailing'). Returns how many were newly tagged. This is the modern 'mark for mailing'.

tools.name: untag_clients
tools.description: Remove a tag (grouping_id) from a selection of clients — explicit client_ids or the same selection filters as list_clients.

tools.name: enroll_clients
tools.description: Enroll a whole selection of clients into an outreach campaign (one prospect per client, using their email on file). Target with client_ids or the list_clients selection filters; campaign_id is the outreach campaign. dry_run=true previews counts without enrolling. Returns enrolled / skipped_no_email / skipped_other / matched. This is how you 'drop a tag into a campaign' — e.g. filter tag=<id> then enroll.

tools.name: make_call_list
tools.description: Load a selection of clients as the call list — the /contacts click-through stack you page through to phone each one. Target with client_ids or the list_clients selection filters (e.g. near_client + radius_miles for 'everyone within 50 miles of this client'). Replaces the current list.

tools.name: list_event_types
tools.description: The bookable packages / event types with prices and durations.

tools.name: create_event_type
tools.description: Create a bookable package / event type (name max 20 chars). price_mode = flat | per_guest (included_participants free, then price_per_participant each) | block (block_size guests per circuit, +block_extra_price per extra circuit) | menu. volunteer_mode = fixed (default_volunteers) | per_circuit (default_volunteers × circuits) | per_participants (1 per default_volunteers guests). requires_prep=true pairs it with a required prep meeting of prep_type_id (another event type id) on the same booking, ending before it starts. stock_qty = how many physical units of this you own (bounce houses, extra photo booths): each date takes that many bookings of it, and they don't block the performer's other bookings; omit/null for a normal show.

tools.name: list_contract_templates
tools.description: Contract templates (client and act kinds) and which is default.

tools.name: set_default_contract_template
tools.description: Make a template the default for its kind.

tools.name: send_signing_link
tools.description: Email the client a link to sign the booking's contract.

tools.name: approve_booking_request
tools.description: Approve a pending online booking request — accept it, confirm the booking (it stops being a quote, so reminders and payment chasing apply), keep the held date, and email the client it's confirmed. The result's `notified` says whether that email actually went. Applies only to bookings that came in through the public booking page and are awaiting a decision (online_approval='pending' on the booking).

tools.name: deny_booking_request
tools.description: Deny a pending online booking request — decline it, free the held date, and email the client it's unavailable.

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: The invoice for a booking: total, paid, balance, payments.

tools.name: email_invoice
tools.description: Email the booking's itemised invoice (PDF) to the client (comms scope).

tools.name: record_payment
tools.description: Record a payment against a booking (money scope).

tools.name: request_payment
tools.description: Email/text the client a secure link to pay online (money scope). type='deposit' (Stripe Connect deposit; optional amount overrides the configured default) or 'balance' (open balance via the client portal). email/sms pick channels (default email).

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: The SMS inbox: one row per client with unread counts.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: One SMS conversation thread by client id.

tools.name: send_text
tools.description: Text a client (comms scope). Pass dry_run=true to preview without sending. US/Canada numbers only unless the account has other countries switched on, and each account has a daily and monthly text limit (lower in its first month) — a 429 with code sms_daily_cap / sms_monthly_cap / sms_international means nothing was sent. Texts go out from the account's OWN texting number: a 409 sms_no_number means it has none yet — call setup_texting_number first.

tools.name: get_texting_number
tools.description: The account's own texting (SMS) number, or — when it has none yet — whether one can be set up and why not. Every account texts from a number of its own; nothing is sent until it has one.

tools.name: setup_texting_number
tools.description: Set up the account's own texting number (comms scope; the login must be allowed to manage outreach/purchases). ActBook buys a local number near the business and registers it with the carriers — a few seconds. A dedicated texting number is a $5/month add-on, which this adds to the account's bill (comped accounts and ones that already have a number are not charged). Safe to call again: an account that already has a number just gets it back. Only do this when the user wants to text clients.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send a general email — an answer to an enquiry or any message the user asks for (comms scope). Sent from the account's own return address. Give a client_id (uses their email on file, and logs the email to their history) or an explicit `to` address. body is plain text unless html=true. dry_run=true previews without sending.

tools.name: list_inquiries
tools.description: Leads from the contact form. Filter by status (new|read|converted|archived|spam).

tools.name: reply_to_inquiry
tools.description: Email a reply to a lead/enquiry (comms scope); marks it read. A reply to an OUTREACH lead (someone who answered a cold email) goes out from the mailbox that emailed them, in the same email thread, and their next answer comes back into ActBook; the result's `from` says which address was used and `note` explains a fallback (that mailbox paused or disconnected). mailbox_id picks a different From. Optionally pass client_id to log the reply to that client's history. dry_run=true previews, including the From.

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: Every automation: the pre-event check-in email (sent a set number of days BEFORE the gig, offset_days negative; default a week before), the day-of SMS, thank-you email, review request and next-year re-book email (each with its timing, template and mailbox_id = the 'Send from' mailbox, null = team default), the payment chase (balance reminders: master on/off, send hour, sender, and six stages due_soon/due_tomorrow/overdue/overdue_7/overdue_14/overdue_30 with offset_days relative to the event day and their subject/body), the contract chase (re-emails the signing link when a contract was sent but not signed: master on/off, send hour, sender, and three stages first/second/final with offset_days = days AFTER the contract was sent), and the mailboxes automations may send from. The re-book email is timed lead_value lead_unit BEFORE the anniversary of the date the booking was made (not the gig date) — the same rule list_rebooking uses.

tools.name: update_automation
tools.description: Change an automation. type is preevent_email, day_of_sms, thankyou_email, review_request, rebook_email or payment_chase. For the gig automations: enabled, offset_days (days from the gig: negative = before, so preevent_email the check-in email uses e.g. offset_days -7 for a week before; 0 = the day; positive = after), send_hour, subject, body, mailbox_id (a sender id from list_automations; 0/null = team default). For rebook_email set lead_value + lead_unit (days|weeks|months) = send that long before the anniversary of the booking date (offset_days is ignored for it); this also moves who appears as due on the Repeat Business board. For payment_chase: enabled, send_hour, mailbox_id and stages — an object keyed by stage, e.g. {"due_soon":{"offset_days":-14},"overdue_30":{"enabled":false}} (offset_days negative = before the event day; pre-due stages must be <= 0, past-due >= 1, enabled stages in order). Chase merge tags: {{first_name}} {{company_name}} {{balance}} {{due_date}} {{pay_link}} {{project}}. For contract_chase (auto re-send the signing link until the contract is signed): enabled, send_hour, mailbox_id and stages — object keyed by first/second/final, each {enabled, offset_days = days AFTER the contract was sent (1-180, enabled stages in ascending order), subject, body}; merge tags {{first_name}} {{company_name}} {{project}} {{sign_link}} {{event_date}} {{sent_date}}. A blank subject/body restores the standard wording.

tools.name: list_outreach
tools.description: Cold-email outreach campaigns.

tools.name: list_broadcasts
tools.description: Email broadcasts to your OWN clients (newsletters / announcements), with their open/click stats. Different from outreach, which is cold email to prospects.

tools.name: get_broadcast
tools.description: One broadcast with its results (sent, opened, clicked, unsubscribed, bounced).

tools.name: create_broadcast
tools.description: Create a DRAFT email broadcast to a segment of your clients. segment is a ClientSelect filter object, e.g. {"tag":12,"state":"MI","near_zip":"48104","radius_miles":50,"q":"library","has_email":true}; omit it to reach all contactable clients. Use {{first_name}} in the subject/body. Does NOT send — call send_broadcast.

tools.name: send_broadcast
tools.description: Send (or schedule) a draft broadcast to its segment (comms scope). Resolves the audience, skipping no-email and unsubscribed addresses. scheduled_at (optional, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') sends later; omit to send now.

tools.name: list_sending_domains
tools.description: Your self-serve sending domains (bought through ActBook) and the mailboxes provisioned on each, with warm-up health. These are ActBook-operated M365 mailboxes used for cold outreach — different from mailboxes you connected yourself. While one is still warming up it only sends for a campaign that names it (set_campaign_mailboxes); a campaign set to use all mailboxes picks it up once warm-up has finished.

tools.name: search_domain
tools.description: Check whether a domain is available to buy for sending (and its $/yr price), with available alternatives if it's taken. Does NOT buy it — call buy_domain.

tools.name: buy_domain
tools.description: Buy a domain for sending and begin its setup (registers it, attaches it to the sending tenant, writes mail DNS). Checks the domain is still available, then charges the yearly domain fee to the card on file right away (refunded automatically if registration fails; fails cleanly with no charge if the card is declined). Returns the domain with its setup status; poll get_sending_domain until status is 'configured', then add_sending_mailbox. Agent plan.

tools.name: connect_sending_domain
tools.description: Connect a domain or subdomain the customer ALREADY owns (registered at GoDaddy/Cloudflare/etc.) for sending — no domain purchase, no domain charge. A dedicated subdomain (e.g. go.theirband.com) is strongly recommended: it keeps their main email and root-domain reputation untouched. We attach it to the sending tenant and return the DNS records they must add at their registrar; poll sending_domain_dns for the exact records + live present/missing status, and get_sending_domain to advance setup. WARNING: a bare root domain they already use for email will have its mail disrupted when its MX is pointed to us. Agent plan.

tools.name: get_sending_domain
tools.description: Advance and read one sending domain's setup state (registration → added → verified → configured). Call after buy_domain/connect_sending_domain until it reports 'configured'.

tools.name: sending_domain_dns
tools.description: For a bring-your-own (connected) domain: the exact DNS records the customer must add at their registrar, each with a live present/missing check (host, type, value, and whether it's visible in public DNS yet). Use this to tell the customer what's left to add and confirm their setup is correct.

tools.name: add_sending_mailbox
tools.description: Provision a mailbox on a configured sending domain (orders an Exchange seat, creates the box, drops it into the warm-up pool. Once warm-up finishes it sends cold email for any campaign that uses all mailboxes; to start it gently earlier, add it to a campaign with set_campaign_mailboxes). local_part = the part before @ (e.g. 'hello'). Charges the first part-month to the card on file immediately — if the card is declined nothing is ordered — then the monthly per-mailbox fee from the next renewal. Each account has a mailbox limit (lower during its first month) and a per-domain limit; a 400 provision_error explains which was reached. Agent plan.

tools.name: cancel_sending_mailbox
tools.description: Cancel a sending mailbox. Stops at the END of the paid period — it keeps working and warming until then, then the box is torn down and the $10/mo stops. id = the sending domain's id, mailbox_id = the mailbox.

tools.name: cancel_sending_domain
tools.description: Cancel a sending domain: cancels all its mailboxes (at period end) and turns off auto-renew, so the domain lapses at expiry. If the customer wants to keep the domain, call transfer_out_domain first.

tools.name: transfer_out_domain
tools.description: Hand a sending domain to the customer: unlocks it and returns the transfer authorization (EPP) code to give their own registrar. Also turns off auto-renew.

tools.name: add_broadcast_image
tools.description: Upload an image for a broadcast email and get back a permanent public URL to embed in the body_html (). image_base64 = the image bytes base64-encoded (or a data: URI); mime = image/jpeg|png|gif|webp (auto-detected if omitted). Max 6 MB.

tools.name: get_subscribe_form
tools.description: Your public 'join my mailing list' signup form: the shareable link + embed URL, which tag new subscribers land in, and the current list size. Share the link to grow the list; broadcast to them with create_broadcast using that tag.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: All account settings (company info, booking config, labels). Includes account_mode: 'performer' (the full booking app) or 'general' (a leads-only account for non-performers — capture + follow-up, no acts/shows).

tools.name: find_setting
tools.description: Find WHERE a setting is, WHAT it does, and HOW to reach it. Search the curated settings catalog by plain language (e.g. 'reply-to email', 'deposits', 'travel time', 'white label', 'timezone', 'api keys'). Each result has a one-line explanation, the page it lives on, and a deep_link that lands on the exact control. Omit q to list every setting. Use this instead of guessing which page a setting is on.

tools.name: get_meeting_settings
tools.description: Discovery-call meeting settings: whether a 'request a call' link is enabled, the video provider (zoom|google_meet|manual), the static meeting link, length, topic, and pad_travel (whether offered slots guard each show's setup, teardown & travel time). Use {{meeting_link}} in an outreach step to invite prospects to book a call.

tools.name: set_meeting_settings
tools.description: Turn on and configure the 'request a call' link (write scope). enabled=true; provider = zoom | google_meet | manual (the tenant's choice); link = a static video link (a Zoom Personal Meeting Room or standing Google Meet) used until auto-generated per-call links are connected; minutes; topic; pad_travel=true hides slots across each gig's full footprint — load-in (setup), teardown, and the real drive to/from the venue (needs a home base + maps key, else falls back to the availability buffer). Then put {{meeting_link}} in an outreach step.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Update account settings, e.g. {company_name, return_email}. company_name is the business name clients see (portal, booking form, contracts, emails). The 'Email signing link' email wording: sign_email_subject, sign_email_message (above the sign button), sign_email_signoff — merge tags {client} {contact} {first_name} {project} {company}; empty string = standard wording. convenience_fee_pct adds a card convenience fee (0–15%) on top of client card payments at checkout (0 = off). Logo/signature images: use set_branding. account_mode = 'performer' | 'general' switches the account between the full booking app and a leads-only (non-performer) surface.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: Login users on the account. Each user has type ('full' or 'limited'); a limited user also has permissions (tool area => full|view) and `access` in words.

tools.name: list_team
tools.description: Performers/staff who can be assigned to gigs.

tools.name: add_team_member
tools.description: Add a performer/staff member.

tools.name: list_assignments
tools.description: Who is assigned to a gig date (pass project_date_id).

tools.name: assign_to_gig
tools.description: Assign a team member to a gig date. Optionally set the commission/split payout for this assignment: pay_type = flat (pay_amount dollars) | hourly (pay_amount per hour of the shift) | percent (pay_amount percent of the gig's booking revenue); pay_amount is the dollar/hourly/percent figure. Omitting them keeps any existing payout. Read these back with get_payouts (Agency 'splits').

tools.name: update_assignment
tools.description: Update an existing gig-date assignment's times or commission/split payout (pay_type = flat|hourly|percent, pay_amount). Identify it by manager_id + project_date_id.

tools.name: get_payouts
tools.description: Commission & split report (Agency 'splits' feature): per-performer payout, the booking revenue their gigs represent, and the agency margin (revenue − payouts), plus summary totals, over a date range. from/to = YYYY-MM-DD (default the current month).

tools.name: list_rebooking
tools.description: Past clients due (or coming up) to re-book. A client's re-book date is the account's re-book timing (lead_value lead_unit, default 30 days) BEFORE the anniversary of the date they made their last booking — events book months ahead, so that's when next year gets planned. Returns 'due' (re-book date within two weeks either side of today) and 'upcoming' (next 60 days), each client with last gig date, booked_on, value, anniversary, rebook_date, days_until_rebook and the nudge status (sent / dismissed / converted), plus the timing in force. Change the timing with update_automation type=rebook_email. Use nudge_rebooking to reach out.

tools.name: nudge_rebooking
tools.description: Send a past client the one-tap re-book message now (same wording and 'Send from' mailbox as the automated re-book email/text, else the account's team default mailer or texting number). Idempotent per anniversary: calling it again for a client already nudged for their current last booking is a no-op that reports the earlier send.

tools.name: dismiss_rebooking
tools.description: Mark a past client as not worth a re-book nudge right now (no message is sent); removes them from the active re-book list for their current last booking.

tools.name: list_reviews
tools.description: Reputation overview: summary stats (requests sent, rated, average stars, promoters/detractors, testimonials published), the configured public review destinations, and recent review requests with their rating, outcome and any private feedback. Reviews are collected by the review_request automation a couple of days after each gig.

tools.name: request_review
tools.description: Send a client a review request for one booking right now (same tokenised star-rating link as the automated post-gig request; happy clients are routed to your public profiles, unhappy ones to private feedback). Idempotent per booking.

tools.name: add_review_destination
tools.description: Add a public review profile clients who rate 4-5 stars are sent to (e.g. label 'Google', url of your Google review link). Manage these to steer happy clients to the platforms that matter to you.

tools.name: list_insurance
tools.description: Insurance / COI vault (Agent+ 'coi' feature): the account's stored policies (certificate of insurance, general liability, workers' comp, licence) with carrier, number, coverage, dates and a lapse flag (expiry_window: 60/30/7/expired). Use send_coi to get one to a venue.

tools.name: add_insurance_policy
tools.description: Add a policy to the insurance vault. type = coi|liability|workers_comp|license|other; optionally carrier, policy_number, coverage_amount, effective_date, expiry_date (YYYY-MM-DD), notes. To attach the document, pass file_base64 (a PDF/JPG/PNG) + file_name.

tools.name: send_coi
tools.description: Email a venue the certificate of insurance for a stored policy, with a cover letter naming them as additional insured. Needs the policy's id (from list_insurance) and venue_email; optionally venue_name, additional_insured wording, and booking_id to tie it to a gig.

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: Document & media locker (Agent+ 'coi' feature): the account's sendable business documents — W-9, publicity photos, contract rider, stage plot, bio, press kit, logo, set list, direct-deposit form and more. Each has a category, a title, and either a stored file or an external link. Filter by category (w9|photo|rider|stage_plot|tech_spec|bio|press_kit|logo|setlist|ach|other). Use send_assets to email one or several to a client.

tools.name: add_asset
tools.description: Add a document/media item to the locker. category = w9|photo|rider|stage_plot|tech_spec|bio|press_kit|logo|setlist|ach|other; optional title and notes. Provide EITHER file_base64 (a PDF/JPG/PNG/GIF/WebP, up to 25 MB) + file_name, OR link_url (for a big gallery / EPK).

tools.name: send_assets
tools.description: Email one or more stored locker documents to a client/venue in one message (e.g. W-9 + rider + stage plot). asset_ids = the ids from list_assets; recipient_email required; optional recipient_name, a message to include, and booking_id to tie it to a gig. Files go as attachments, link items are listed inline.

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Archive a locker document by id (soft — it stops appearing and can't be sent).

tools.name: list_contract_clauses
tools.description: Reusable contract paragraphs (clauses) and where they apply.

tools.name: create_contract_clause
tools.description: Add a reusable contract clause (title max 50 chars).

tools.name: list_letters
tools.description: Reusable email/letter bodies; one may be the default.

tools.name: create_letter
tools.description: Add a reusable letter/email body (title max 30 chars). Set default=true to make it the default.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: A client's (or booking's) notes / history — the comments log shown on the client page. Pass client_id or booking_id.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a note to a CLIENT's history (shows on the client page) or to a booking — e.g. log a call, an inquiry reply, or what was agreed. Pass client_id (and/or booking_id) and comment. contact_id (optional) ties the note to the person at the client it is about; it must be one of that client's contacts. Use this (or add_client_note) to put a note on a client — add_project_note is a shared notepad not tied to any client.

tools.name: list_project_notes
tools.description: The shared notepad; handled=done.

tools.name: add_project_note
tools.description: Add a note to the account's shared notepad (a general team scratchpad, NOT attached to any client or booking). To note something on a client, use add_comment (or add_client_note) instead.

tools.name: list_todos
tools.description: To-dos. Pass done=false for open items only.

tools.name: create_todo
tools.description: Create a to-do (item max 50 chars; longer text in details). Optionally tie it to a booking/client, set due_date ('YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') and urgent. contact_id (optional) ties it to the person at that client to follow up with. It lands on the dashboard of the user this key belongs to, or assign_to (a teammate's login or user_id); is_global shows it to everyone.

tools.name: get_branding
tools.description: The account's logo (printed at the top of contracts and invoices) and each user's signature image (printed on contracts they book).

tools.name: set_branding
tools.description: Set the contract/site logo, the high-res print logo for QR posters, or a user's signature image. what='logo' or 'signature' (PNG, JPG or GIF, max 2 MB) or 'poster_logo' (PNG, JPG, GIF or SVG, max 5 MB — SVG is sanitized). Give an https url OR base64 data. For a signature, user_id defaults to this key's user.

tools.name: complete_todo
tools.description: Mark a to-do done.

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: The account's sending/receiving email accounts (secrets hidden). Each also says can_send, outreach_ready (may carry cold email for a campaign that uses all mailboxes today), needs_pool (bought through ActBook and still warming: only sends for a campaign that names it) and bounce_visibility: inbox | graph | forwarded (ActBook learns about its bounces) or none (it does not — the mailbox is held to 20 cold emails a day until bounce notices are forwarded to an inbound address). Also provider (google | microsoft | yahoo | other — used for provider matching) and send_gap_min (its own gap between two cold emails; null = automatic).

tools.name: create_user
tools.description: Create a login user (password min 8 chars; email required — sign-in is by email). Needs a connection holding write + money + comms, made by a user allowed to manage users. TWO KINDS: (1) a FULL user: access_level 1-5 (you can only create logins below your own level; is_admin for full access). (2) a LIMITED user: type='limited' plus either preset (booth_staff | performer | office_assistant | bookkeeper | marketing) or permissions, an object of tool area => 'full' or 'view' (areas: tradeshows, calendar, bookings, clients, contracts, payments, inbox, outreach, reports, website; 'view' exists for calendar, bookings and clients only). Tools that another tool needs are added automatically and the saved set is returned — e.g. to add someone who can ONLY use the trade-show tools: type='limited', preset='booth_staff'. A limited user never reaches settings, users, billing or API keys, and counts as a plan seat. See list_user_permissions for the areas, what each needs and what each preset ticks. Limit to certain acts: act_restricted=true + act_ids (the performer preset sets act_restricted for you — still send act_ids).

tools.name: delete_booking
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a booking.

tools.name: list_payments
tools.description: Payments recorded against a booking.

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: One client with its contacts (names, emails, phones) and its 10 most recent notes (recent_comments).

tools.name: update_client
tools.description: Update a client's name/address/city/state/zip, and set a client-level email/phone (used for invoices/payment links when a booking has no contact email). Optional note appends a note to the client's history (same as add_client_note).

tools.name: add_client_note
tools.description: Add a note to a client's record — it shows in the client's notes/history on the client page, dated and attributed. Use it to log calls, emails/inquiry replies, what was quoted or agreed, follow-ups. id = the client id. Optional booking_id ties it to one of their bookings too; optional contact_id ties it to the person at the client it is about (one of this client's contacts).

tools.name: delete_client
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a client.

tools.name: find_duplicates
tools.description: Find likely-duplicate client pairs (same name & location, a shared email, or a shared phone). Returns each pair with both records, their booking counts, the match reason(s), and a suggested survivor (suggest_keep). Feed a pair to merge_clients: id = the one to absorb, into = the one to keep (use suggest_keep).

tools.name: merge_clients
tools.description: Merge a duplicate client into another. id = the duplicate to absorb (it is archived/soft-deleted); into = the surviving client_id to keep. Moves the duplicate's bookings, contacts, comments, todos and groupings onto the survivor. Use this to fix a booking created under a new/duplicate client instead of the existing one, or to clean up a pair from find_duplicates.

tools.name: list_client_bookings
tools.description: The bookings/quotes for a client.

tools.name: list_client_documents
tools.description: List the documents attached to a client (e.g. scanned contracts). Each has a download link via get_document_download.

tools.name: upload_client_document
tools.description: Attach a document to a client (write scope). Give a public https `url` to fetch, OR base64 `data` with a `filename`. Optional `content_type` and `description`. Stored privately; max 25MB; PDF/images/Word/Excel/text.

tools.name: get_document_download
tools.description: Get a short-lived (5 minute) download URL for a client document by its doc id.

tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Remove a client document (soft-delete, write scope).

tools.name: add_contact
tools.description: Add a contact (name/email/phone) to a client.

tools.name: update_contact
tools.description: Edit a contact's name, email or phone (email/phone stored in contact_info). email_bad=true marks the contact's email as bad (bounced, or the wrong person) so mailings skip it, and false clears the mark; email_bad_address limits that to one address when the contact has several. Changing email to a different address clears the mark.

tools.name: delete_contact
tools.description: Remove a contact from a client.

tools.name: list_acts
tools.description: The performer acts/catalog with day rate and travel settings.

tools.name: create_act
tools.description: Add a performer act (name max 50 chars).

tools.name: update_act
tools.description: Update a performer act.

tools.name: delete_act
tools.description: Delete a performer act.

tools.name: update_event_type
tools.description: Update a bookable package/event type. See create_event_type for price_mode, volunteer_mode and requires_prep/prep_type_id.

tools.name: delete_event_type
tools.description: Delete a bookable package/event type.

tools.name: create_outreach
tools.description: Create a cold-email outreach campaign (draft). Open/click tracking is OFF unless tracking_enabled=true: tracking adds a hidden image and sends links through actbook.app, which makes cold email likelier to land in spam; replies are counted either way.

tools.name: get_outreach
tools.description: One outreach campaign with its steps, and 'sending': what its mailboxes can deliver a day at their gaps (reachable_per_day, limit_reachable), each mailbox's daily limit / gap / provider, and the mail providers its leads are on (lead_providers, lead_provider_note).

tools.name: set_outreach_status
tools.description: Set a campaign's status: draft, active (starts the drip — comms scope) or paused. Activating runs the pre-launch checklist first: if the campaign isn't ready it returns 422 not_ready with a 'blockers' list (fix each, e.g. no leads / no sending mailbox / no mailing address / bad send window) — call outreach_preflight to see them without launching.

tools.name: outreach_preflight
tools.description: Pre-launch checklist for a campaign WITHOUT launching it. Returns {ok, blockers[], warnings[]}. Blockers (ok=false) stop a launch: missing copy/subject, no leads, no healthy sending mailbox, an invalid send window, or no physical mailing address. Warnings don't block but advise: a still-warming or brand-new sending domain, a mailbox whose bounces ActBook cannot see (bounces_unseen), a bought mailbox still warming that is sitting this campaign out (provisioned_warming), missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC, unverified/risky leads, blank merge fields. Call this before set_outreach_status active.

tools.name: update_outreach
tools.description: Update a campaign's schedule + sender (any subset): tracking_enabled (bool; open/click tracking — off by default, on adds a hidden image and sends links through actbook.app, which hurts cold-email deliverability), daily_cap, send_hour_start/send_hour_end (0-23, in its timezone), timezone (e.g. 'America/Chicago'), send_days (CSV of ISO weekdays, 1=Mon..7=Sun), start_date (YYYY-MM-DD; no sends before it), skip_holidays (bool, US federal holidays), stop_on_reply_domain (bool; one reply from a company pauses every other lead at that same email domain), footer_text (your sign-off line; the unsubscribe link + mailing address are always appended regardless), recipient_domain_daily_cap (max sends to the same recipient email domain per day; 0 = no limit — avoids flooding one company), token_defaults (a {token: value} map of merge-field fallbacks used when a lead's own field is blank, e.g. {"company":"your company","city":"your area"}, so {{company}} never renders as an empty gap; {{first_name}} already falls back to "there"; send {} to clear), name, from_name, from_email, reply_to. hold_new_leads (bool): true = nobody NEW gets the first email while everyone already emailed still gets their follow-ups (use it to rework the first email without breaking the follow-ups people were promised); false lifts the hold. HOW IT SENDS: emails are spread evenly through the window and never sent in a burst; email_gap_min + random_wait_max = minimum minutes (plus a random extra) between two cold emails from one mailbox (0/null = automatic, which always lets a mailbox reach its daily limit — a longer gap lowers what it can send; get_outreach 'sending' shows whether the limit is still reachable); match_provider (bool) = prefer a Google mailbox for a Google lead and a Microsoft mailbox for a Microsoft lead; text_only (bool) = every email as plain text with no HTML part (cannot be combined with tracking_enabled=true; setting it switches tracking off); first_email_text_only (bool); new_leads_per_day (int, 0/null = no limit) = at most that many new people a day, and that many of the day's limit are held for them; send_order = followups_first | new_first. ooo_pause (bool, on by default) = a lead whose auto-reply says they are out of office is held until the day after they are back (never counted as a reply); placement_weekly (bool) = run an inbox-placement test every week while it is active.

tools.name: set_outreach_steps
tools.description: Set a campaign's email sequence: steps=[{subject, body, delay_days, same_thread?, variants?}]. Subject/body support merge fields ({{first_name}}, {{company}}) and SPINTAX {a|b|c} (picked at random per send — the simplest way to vary wording and dodge spam filters). same_thread=true on a follow-up (step 2+) sends it as a REPLY in the same thread as the prospect's previous email ("Re: <the subject they actually got>", threaded headers) — usually lifts reply rates; leaving a follow-up's subject empty also means same_thread. Step 1 always needs a subject and always starts the thread. Optional variants=[{subject,body,off?}] A/B-test alternative wordings against the primary (on a same_thread step only the body varies); campaign_stats reports open rate per variant. The step's own wording is version A and the variants are B, C, …; "off": true on a variant (or primary_off=true on the step for version A) keeps that version but stops sending it — at least one version always stays on. Setting the steps replaces them, so repeat the off flags or those versions are switched back on.

same_thread.description: Follow-ups only: send as a reply in the same thread as the previous email. Implied when subject is empty.

primary_off.description: Switch version A (this step's own subject/body) off: it is kept but no longer sent. Needs at least one variant that is on.

tools.name: enroll_prospects
tools.description: Enroll prospects into a campaign: prospects=[{email, first_name, ...}]. dry_run=true previews.

tools.name: list_prospects
tools.description: List the leads in a campaign for per-lead management. Optional q (matches email/name/company), status (active|paused|removed|replied|unsubscribed|bounced|completed, or the two views out_of_office = active leads on hold because they sent an out-of-office, and in_branch = active leads inside a branch), page, per_page. Each row has ooo_until (the day they said they are back; they resume the day after) and in_branch/branch_id. Returns rows plus total and a per-status count breakdown.

tools.name: update_prospect
tools.description: Manage one lead (comms scope). status pauses/resumes/removes them (removed = soft delete: kept for history, never emailed again; active resumes). move_to re-enrolls them into another campaign from step 1. out_of_office=false ends an out-of-office hold now ("they are back"). Pass status, move_to and/or out_of_office.

tools.name: get_outreach_branches
tools.description: A campaign's BRANCHES: short sets of emails that start when something happens to a lead. Triggers: no_reply (finished the sequence without replying → e.g. one last note, or a re-approach next season), ooo_return (back from an out-of-office → a welcome-back email, then the main sequence carries on), clicked (clicked a link; needs tracking on → these emails instead of the rest of the sequence), reply_phrase (their reply contained a phrase such as 'next year' and was not a clear no → a re-approach after wait_days; the reply still goes to the pipeline). Each branch has stats {entered, waiting, sent, replied}. A human reply always stops automation; branch emails count toward the campaign's daily limit.

tools.name: save_outreach_branch
tools.description: Create a branch on a campaign (omit branch_id) or replace one (branch_id) — comms scope. trigger = no_reply | ooo_return | clicked | reply_phrase; wait_days = days after the trigger before the first branch email; steps = [{subject?, body, delay_days?, same_thread?, variants?}] (up to 3; an email with no subject is sent in the lead's existing thread); active (bool) switches it on; phrase (reply_phrase only: comma-separated phrases); approved=true is REQUIRED to switch a reply_phrase branch on, because it emails someone again after they replied — only pass it when the user has clearly agreed to that. One active branch per trigger (several reply_phrase branches are fine).

tools.name: delete_outreach_branch
tools.description: Delete a branch (comms scope). Leads waiting in it are released: back to the main sequence for ooo_return / clicked, finished for the others.

tools.name: get_placement_test
tools.description: The latest INBOX-PLACEMENT TEST of a campaign: its first email, sent from each of its sending mailboxes to a few mailboxes ActBook reads, and where each landed — inbox / spam / not found per mailbox and per provider (Google, Microsoft, other), SPF/DKIM/DMARC as the receiver recorded them, and findings in plain words. It is a small sample: a signal, not a guarantee (and Gmail's Promotions tab is not visible to it). seed_mailboxes shows how many test mailboxes exist per provider.

tools.name: run_placement_test
tools.description: Queue an inbox-placement test for a campaign (comms scope). It sends a handful of test emails per sending mailbox over about an hour (each mailbox keeps its usual gap; they count toward the mailbox's daily limit but appear in no campaign number), then reads where they landed — get the result with get_placement_test. Refused while one is running or within 6 hours of the last one.

tools.name: outreach_stats
tools.description: Overall outreach deliverability — emails sent/delivered/bounced/opened/clicked, the prospect funnel (replied/unsubscribed/bounced), and open/reply/bounce rates — plus each connected sending inbox's health (today's volume vs cap, bounce count, and whether it auto-paused). Check this to see if delivery is healthy.

tools.name: campaign_stats
tools.description: One campaign's deliverability + funnel stats and rates.

tools.name: list_outreach_review
tools.description: Suggested next moves for outreach: open cards, each a concrete next move for one campaign that waits for an approval. Kinds: raise_cap (replies are 2%+ and it keeps reaching its daily limit — approve raises the limit by up to 25%, never past what its mailboxes can send), add_mailbox (same, but the mailboxes are full), disable_variant (one A/B version is clearly losing once every version has had enough sends — approve switches it off), no_positive (100+ people emailed and nobody interested — approve holds NEW first emails while follow-ups continue), unsubs / bounces (how many more would trip the automatic safety pause), leads_low (under three sending days of new leads left), segments (a lead category not tried yet, or clearly ahead/behind). Returns {enabled, cards:[{id, campaign_id, kind, severity (warn|good|info), action, approvable, title, detail (what it saw), approve_label, approve_does (exactly what approving changes), if_ignored, metrics}]}. Nothing changes until a card is approved with resolve_outreach_review. If enabled is false, turn it on with set_outreach_review.

tools.name: set_outreach_review
tools.description: Turn outreach suggestions on or off (comms scope). When on, ActBook looks at every live campaign each weekday morning, files a card when there is a well-founded next move and emails the owner once about new ones. It never changes a campaign by itself.

tools.name: run_outreach_review
tools.description: Look at every live or paused campaign right now: file new suggestion cards, bring open ones up to date and close the ones that no longer apply (comms scope). Changes no campaign. Idempotent — one open card per campaign per kind. Returns the number of new cards plus the open cards.

tools.name: resolve_outreach_review
tools.description: Approve or ignore one suggestion card (comms scope). ONLY approve when the user has clearly said yes to that specific suggestion — read them the card's approve_does first. decision='approve' applies the card's action after re-checking the numbers as they are now: raise_cap raises the campaign's daily limit, disable_variant switches one A/B version off, hold_new holds new first emails (follow-ups continue; lift it with update_outreach hold_new_leads=false). If the premise no longer holds, nothing is changed and the reply has applied=false with message saying why. decision='ignore' dismisses it (the same suggestion stays away for two weeks). Returns {action_taken, applied, status, message}. card_id is from list_outreach_review.

tools.name: list_blocklist
tools.description: The account's BLOCK LIST: addresses and whole domains that are never emailed, in any campaign or newsletter. People who unsubscribe, bounce or are checked invalid land here by themselves. Use it to answer 'who unsubscribed' (reason=unsubscribed, optionally campaign_id). Optional q (search), reason = unsubscribed | bounced | invalid | complaint | manual | imported | other, kind = address | domain, campaign_id, limit, offset. Returns {entries:[{id, value, is_domain, reason_label, campaign, note, created_at}], total, counts}.

tools.name: add_to_blocklist
tools.description: Block an address or a WHOLE DOMAIN from ever being emailed: entry='jane@school.org' or entry='school.org' (every address at that domain); entries=[…] for a list. Any live sequence to it is stopped. Optional note.

tools.name: remove_from_blocklist
tools.description: Take one entry off the block list (entry_id from list_blocklist). If the person asked not to be emailed (an unsubscribe or a spam complaint) the call is refused with confirm_required unless confirm=true — ONLY pass confirm=true when the user has clearly said that person asked to hear from them again.

tools.name: set_mailbox_gap
tools.description: Set one mailbox's own gap between two cold emails, in minutes, across every campaign (comms scope): it never sends two closer together than that. minutes=0 or null = automatic (a gap that always lets it reach its daily limit). A long gap lowers how many it can send in a day.

tools.name: set_campaign_mailboxes
tools.description: Set which connected inboxes a campaign rotates its sends across (comms scope). mailbox_ids=[…] from the mailboxes list; an empty list means use all healthy inboxes. Spreading a campaign over several warmed inboxes is how you scale cold volume without burning any one account.

tools.name: set_mailbox_warmup
tools.description: Turn email warm-up on/off for an inbox (comms scope). A new sending inbox should warm up 2-4 weeks before real volume: warm-up slowly ramps its daily cap and sends a little friendly mail to the warm-up pool to build inbox reputation. enabled=true to start.

tools.name: resume_mailbox
tools.description: Resume an inbox that auto-paused (too many bounces/complaints), after you've cleaned the list (comms scope).

tools.name: update_team_member
tools.description: Update a performer/staff member.

tools.name: remove_team_member
tools.description: Remove (soft-delete) a performer/staff member.

tools.name: unassign_from_gig
tools.description: Unassign a team member from a gig date.

tools.name: update_contract_clause
tools.description: Update a reusable contract clause.

tools.name: delete_contract_clause
tools.description: Delete a reusable contract clause.

tools.name: update_letter
tools.description: Update a reusable letter/email body; default=true makes it the default.

tools.name: delete_letter
tools.description: Delete a reusable letter/email body.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.description: Edit an activity note: comment, sticky flag, or contact_id (the person at the client it is about; 0 unties it).

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description: Delete an activity note.

tools.name: update_project_note
tools.description: Edit a shared-notepad note (note text or handled/done flag).

tools.name: delete_project_note
tools.description: Delete a shared-notepad note.

tools.name: update_todo
tools.description: Update a to-do: item, details, due_date, urgent, done, or reassign to a booking/client/gig date. contact_id ties it to a person at its client (0 unties it).

tools.name: delete_todo
tools.description: Delete a to-do.

tools.name: get_mailbox
tools.description: One sending/receiving email account (secrets hidden), incl. warm-up health: warmup.inbox_rate and warmup.placement = where its warm-up mail landed at real Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo inboxes over 14 days (our own-server filler excluded).

tools.name: update_user
tools.description: Update a login user: name, email, password (min 8), enabled; for a FULL user access_level 1-5 and is_admin. Needs a connection holding write + money + comms; only logins below your own access level (owners: anyone). LIMITED USERS: type='limited' with preset or permissions (object of tool area => 'full'|'view'; see list_user_permissions) makes the login limited or replaces its tools — the whole set is replaced, so send every tool they should keep; the saved set is returned. type='full' with access_level makes a limited user a full user again. Nobody can change their own type or tools. Limit to certain acts: act_restricted (bool) + act_ids (array of act ids, replaces the list).

tools.name: list_user_permissions
tools.description: The checklist for LIMITED users: every tool area (key, label, what it covers, whether it has a view-only mode, which other areas it needs) and the presets (booth_staff, performer, office_assistant, bookkeeper, marketing) with what each ticks. Read this before create_user / update_user with type='limited'.

tools.name: delete_user
tools.description: Remove (soft-delete) a login user. Needs a connection holding write + money + comms; only logins below your own access level (owners: anyone).

tools.name: list_blackouts
tools.description: Unavailable date ranges (blackouts) that block online booking.

tools.name: add_blackout
tools.description: Block a date range from online booking (end_date defaults to start_date).

tools.name: remove_blackout
tools.description: Remove a blackout by id.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Outgoing webhook subscriptions (Zapier/integrations).

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Subscribe a URL to events. events is a comma-separated list or 'all'. Returns the signing secret once.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook subscription.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: File a bug report or suggestion for the dev team. type is bug|suggestion; page/steps optional.

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.description: Feedback/bug reports filed on this account.

tools.name: get_inquiry
tools.description: One lead/enquiry in full.

tools.name: set_inquiry_status
tools.description: Set a lead's status (new, read, converted, archived or spam) and/or mark it replied. replied=true records that the lead was answered somewhere else (your own mail app, a call): it stamps the time, shows the replied tick on the Inquiries page and moves a new lead to read; replied=false clears it. Pass status, replied, or both. (reply_to_inquiry sends the email and marks it replied by itself.)

tools.name: list_dates
tools.description: The gig dates on a booking (venue, times, setup, headcount).

tools.name: add_date
tools.description: Add a gig date to a booking. date=YYYY-MM-DD required. Optional: type (event-type id), setup_time/start_time/end_time/done_time (HH:MM), participants, volunteers, venue, address, city, state, zip, phone, timezone, is_public, segment_price, act_id (this date's act — only with 'Book multiple acts per booking' on; else the booking's act).

tools.name: update_date
tools.description: Update a gig date on a booking (any of: date, times, headcount, venue/address, etc.). act_id moves this date to another act (needs 'Book multiple acts per booking' on).

tools.name: delete_date
tools.description: Remove a gig date from a booking.

tools.name: get_contract
tools.description: Render a booking's contract. format=html (default) returns HTML; format=pdf returns the PDF base64-encoded. Optional template_id.

tools.name: send_contract
tools.description: Email the contract PDF to the client (comms scope). Uses the booking's contact email unless you pass email. Optional subject, message, template_id. Stamps contract-sent.

tools.name: mark_contract
tools.description: Stamp or clear a booking's contract status: sent=true/false and/or returned=true/false.

tools.name: update_line_item
tools.description: Update a booking line item (description, price, quantity); the booking total is adjusted to match.

tools.name: update_payment
tools.description: Update a recorded payment on a booking: amount, date (YYYY-MM-DD) or description (money scope).

tools.name: delete_payment
tools.description: Delete a recorded payment from a booking (money scope).

tools.name: get_availability_rules
tools.description: The account's scheduling rules: weekly working hours, min notice, booking window, buffer, max bookings/day.

tools.name: set_availability_rules
tools.description: Update scheduling rules. days = {"0":null,"1":["09:00","21:00"],...} (0=Sun; null=closed). lead_hours (min notice), window_days (how far ahead), buffer_min, max_per_day.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: A detailed report over a date range. name = income | revenue-by-act | average-booking | appearances | conversion | repeat | mileage | business-history. from/to = YYYY-MM-DD (default this year). mileage = one-way + round-trip driving miles from the home base to each gig (tax mileage); distances are cached per date, lookups caps fresh Google lookups per call (default 50) and rows with status=pending fill on the next call. business-history = the whole life of the business, one row per year (ignores from/to): performed that year by gig date (total fees, bookings, gigs, averages, year-over-year change), booked that year by booking date, booking balance (booked − performed) and the running 'on the books' total; status is complete | so_far (the current year) | booked_ahead (future years with gigs). Lost bookings are left out unless include_lost=true.

tools.name: list_referrals
tools.description: Network gig referrals. type=pool (open gigs from other performers, default), mine (gigs you referred), or claims (gigs you claimed, with client details).

tools.name: refer_gig
tools.description: Refer one of your bookings to the ActBook network for another performer to claim. Requires network opt-in.

tools.name: claim_referral
tools.description: Claim an open network referral; returns the client's contact details. Requires network opt-in.

tools.name: get_partner_earnings
tools.description: This account's ActBook referral link (and the link its QR code carries) and what the partner programme has earned it: link clicks, QR scans, sign-ups, paying customers, commission earned / still in the 30-day wait / ready to pay out / paid, the next payout date, and each referred account by business name with what it earned. Read-only. A partner earns 20% of what an account they referred pays for its plan in its first 12 months, paid by PayPal once a month from $50. An ActBook subscriber who refers ALSO earns 10% of the referred plan's price as an ongoing ActBook-Bucks credit on their own bill, for as long as both accounts stay subscribed (on top of the first-year cash); a non-subscriber partner earns the first-year cash only. Joining (signing the agreement, PayPal address) is done by a person on the Refer page (/refer); payouts are made by ActBook and cannot be requested here. enabled=false means the cash programme is not open yet; joined=false means the agreement has not been signed.

tools.name: list_api_activity
tools.description: The account's API call log: what its API keys and connected apps (this connector included) have called, newest first. Each entry: time (UTC), which key or connector, whether it came through the API or an MCP tool (with the tool's name), method, path, query string, HTTP status, caller IP and how long it took. Request and response contents are never recorded. key_id = only that API key (ids are on the API keys page); credential = key or oauth (connected apps); before = an entry id, to page back; limit up to 200 (default 100). Kept 90 days. Read-only; account owner or a user who manages settings.

tools.name: withdraw_referral
tools.description: Withdraw one of your own still-open network referrals.

tools.name: list_gift_certificates
tools.description: Gift certificates. redeemed=0 (open, default), 1 (redeemed) or all.

tools.name: get_gift_certificate
tools.description: One gift certificate by number.

tools.name: issue_gift_certificate
tools.description: Issue a gift certificate (money scope). amount required; optional code, purchaser, recipient, paid_amount, paid_by, comments.

tools.name: update_gift_certificate
tools.description: Update a gift certificate (money scope): redeemed=true (+booking_id) to mark used, redeemed=false to clear; or edit recipient/purchaser/comments.

tools.name: list_waivers
tools.description: Signed liability waivers (agent/agency add-on). Filter by status (signed/void/spam) or q (name/email/phone/child). Each row includes its pass_url.

tools.name: get_waiver
tools.description: One signed waiver by id, with its pass URL.

tools.name: void_waiver
tools.description: Void a signed waiver (status=void) or restore it (status=signed).

tools.name: list_waiver_templates
tools.description: The account's waiver wording — one active adult and one minor template, with version hashes.

tools.name: save_waiver_template
tools.description: Create or update a waiver template (one active per kind). kind=individual|minor; body_html is the wording (basic HTML); re-stamps the version hash.

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: The tenant's free website: its content document (pages/sections), publish status, the live + preview URLs, available section types, a summary of the live data the site pulls in (company name, bookable packages, booking link), and (sites) the list of all this tenant's sites with their act_id. Read this first before editing. Optional act_id edits a per-act site instead of the primary one (Agency tenants only; act_id 0/omitted = the primary site).

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Replace the whole website content document (write scope). GET it first with get_site, edit the config, send it back here. Sections are typed: hero, about, services (auto-pulls the tenant's bookable packages), gallery, logos (a small grayscale 'Trusted by' row of client logos: heading + up to 12 images + optional names), video, testimonials, faq, booking-cta, contact. Never use a client logo as a hero or gallery photo. Rich text (about body, faq answers) supports a safe markdown subset (**bold**, *italic*, [text](url)). Saves a DRAFT — call publish_site to go live. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: add_site_section
tools.description: Add one section to the home page (write scope). type is one of hero/about/services/gallery/logos/video/testimonials/faq/booking-cta/contact (logos = a 'Trusted by' row of client logos: {heading, images[], names[]}); data holds that section's fields; optional after=<section id> to position it. Saves a draft. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: update_site_section
tools.description: Edit one section by id (write scope): merge new fields into its data, and/or enable/disable it. Saves a draft. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: remove_site_section
tools.description: Remove a section by id (write scope). Saves a draft. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: preview_site
tools.description: Render the current draft to the preview URL (write scope) so the tenant can review before publishing. Returns the preview_url. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Publish the current draft LIVE to the tenant's website (write scope). Returns the live_url. Do this only after the tenant is happy with the draft/preview. Optional act_id publishes a per-act site (Agency only); each act's site has its own slug/URL.

tools.name: upload_site_media
tools.description: Add an image to the tenant's website media library (write scope). Pass a public https image 'url' (it's fetched and self-hosted) OR base64 image 'data' (jpeg/png/webp/avif/gif, up to 10MB). Returns a /media/… path — use it as the image/images field of a hero, about or gallery section. Only upload media the tenant owns or is licensed to use. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: list_site_media
tools.description: List the images already uploaded to the tenant's website, as /media paths + urls. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: set_site_theme
tools.description: Switch the site's visual theme (write scope). Options: 'aurora' (dark, modern, gradient — tech-y/nightlife), 'editorial' (warm serif, photo-led magazine — circus/variety/speakers/most performers), 'clean' (light, minimal, lots of whitespace — speakers/corporate), 'spotlight' (bold full-bleed photo hero, condensed display — DJs/bands/circus), 'playful' (bright, rounded, fun — kids' entertainers/party acts). Branding colours overlay any theme. Optional act_id targets a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: import_site
tools.description: Build the tenant's ActBook site by importing their EXISTING website (WordPress, Squarespace, plain HTML…). Pulls their title, bio, video, performer photos (hero + gallery) and contact into a structured DRAFT (editorial theme) and self-hosts the images; client logos are kept out of the photos and go to a 'logos' row. Review/edit the result with get_site, then publish_site. Does NOT publish automatically. Great first step when a performer already has a site. The response includes a rights notice — the tenant is responsible for having the rights to any imported images/text; only publish media they own or are licensed to use. Optional act_id imports into a per-act site (Agency only).

tools.name: set_mailbox_default
tools.description: Choose which mailbox Compose/replies send FROM (write scope). team_default=true makes it the tenant's shared fallback From (not allowed on a personal mailbox). my_default=true makes it THIS key's own default From (a shared or your personal mailbox, overriding the team default for you); my_default=false clears your personal default. List mailboxes first with list_mailboxes.

tools.name: list_inbox
tools.description: The email inbox: messages forwarded into ActBook. scope=all (your personal + shared, default), mine, shared, or spam. unread=true to show only unread; limit caps rows. Returns unread + spam counts too.

tools.name: get_inbox_message
tools.description: One inbox message by id, including its full body text.

tools.name: triage_inbox_message
tools.description: Triage an inbox message (write scope): read=true/false (mark read/unread), spam=true/false (move to/from spam), client_id=<id> to link it to a client or null to unlink, box='shared'|'me'|<user_id> to move it to the shared inbox, your own, or a teammate's personal inbox. Pass any combination.

tools.name: delete_inbox_message
tools.description: Permanently delete one inbox message (write scope).

tools.name: reply_to_inbox_message
tools.description: Reply to the sender of an inbox message (comms scope). body is the reply text; it threads and quotes the original. Optional mailbox_id picks the From (else your default sender — or, when the message is a lead's answer in a cold-email conversation, the mailbox that emailed them; `note` in the result says so). dry_run=true previews without sending.

tools.name: create_client_from_inbox
tools.description: Create a new client from an inbox message's sender (write scope) and link the message to it. Returns the new client_id.

tools.name: mark_all_inbox_read
tools.description: Mark every message visible to this key as read (write scope).

tools.name: empty_inbox_spam
tools.description: Permanently delete all spam visible to this key (write scope). Returns how many were removed.

tools.name: list_inbound_addresses
tools.description: The @in.actbook.app forward targets for this tenant — each maps to a shared inbox (whole team) or a personal one (a single user). Forward a real mailbox to one of these to pull its mail into ActBook.

tools.name: add_inbound_address
tools.description: Claim a new @in.actbook.app forward target (write scope). localpart is the bit before @ (globally unique — try company-user if taken). owner='shared' (default, whole team) or 'me' (this key's user, personal). Optional label.

tools.name: remove_inbound_address
tools.description: Remove an @in.actbook.app forward target by id (write scope).

tools.name: get_pipeline
tools.description: The booking pipeline as lifecycle lanes (Proposal sent [lane key 'quote'], Contract & deposit [key 'contract'], Confirmed, Balance due, Lost). Each lane lists its bookings with totals, paid and balance; Contract & deposit bookings carry open_steps — any of send_contract (your move), awaiting_signature, deposit_due. Stage is computed from the booking's state.

tools.name: mark_booking_lost
tools.description: Mark a booking as lost/declined (moves it to the Lost lane).

tools.name: reopen_booking
tools.description: Reopen a lost booking (clears the lost/cancelled mark).

tools.name: waive_booking_contract
tools.description: Waive the contract requirement on a booking, so it skips the Contract lane.

tools.name: unwaive_booking_contract
tools.description: Undo a contract waiver on a booking (it expects a contract again).

tools.name: list_support_tickets
tools.description: This account's support tickets (to the ActBook team) with status and last activity.

tools.name: get_support_ticket
tools.description: One support ticket with its full message thread.

tools.name: open_support_ticket
tools.description: Open a new support ticket with the ActBook support team (notifies a human agent).

tools.name: reply_support_ticket
tools.description: Add a reply/message to one of this account's support tickets.

tools.name: list_trade_shows
tools.description: The tenant's trade-show QR booth sign-ups: each has a public_url + token to print as a QR code, an optional linked follow-up campaign, instant-SMS settings, poster_cta (the QR-poster call-to-action), active + archived flags and lead count. Archived shows are hidden unless include_archived=true.

tools.name: create_trade_show
tools.description: Create a trade-show booth sign-up (available on every plan). name required. Optional campaign_id links a follow-up outreach sequence (must belong to this account; needs the outreach plan to actually send). sms_enabled + sms_message fire an instant text to each scan. poster_cta is the line printed under the QR code (default "Scan to book us!"). Returns the token and public_url for the QR code.

tools.name: update_trade_show
tools.description: Update a trade show: name, campaign_id (0 to unlink), sms_enabled, sms_message, poster_cta (the QR-poster call-to-action), active (false pauses it), archived (true hides it from the main list and stops capture — reversible; false restores it).

tools.name: delete_trade_show
tools.description: Delete a trade show permanently. To just get a finished show out of the way (reversibly), use update_trade_show with archived=true instead.

tools.name: get_booth_staff_link
tools.description: A trade show's booth staff link: the link + PIN that lets temporary helpers WITHOUT an ActBook login capture leads for that one show from their own phone (available on every plan; no user seat). Returns state (active/paused/expired), when it closes, the url and pin, and who has signed in with how many leads each. staff_link is null when the show has none.

tools.name: create_booth_staff_link
tools.description: Make (or replace) a trade show's booth staff link. last_day (YYYY-MM-DD, the show's last day; default today, at most 60 days ahead) — the link closes by itself at 3 AM the next morning, account time. Returns url + pin to hand to the helpers. Replacing an existing link signs every phone out at once, so only do it when the user asks for a new link or PIN.

tools.name: revoke_booth_staff_link
tools.description: Turn a trade show's booth staff link off now. Every helper's phone is signed out immediately and leads they have not uploaded yet will not come through. Leads already uploaded stay in the pipeline.

tools.name: list_booth_captures
tools.description: Recent booth captures synced from the field: the entered/OCR'd contact fields (name/email/phone/company/title), notes, OCR + transcript status, and the pipeline inquiry_id each created. Optional trade_show_id filters to one show; limit caps rows.

tools.name: get_booth_capture
tools.description: One booth capture by id, with its contact fields, notes, enrichment status and linked inquiry_id.

tools.name: get_follow_up
tools.description: The warm lead-follow-up sequence (available on every plan): the emails that auto-send to the leads you capture at a booth/show, from your own mailbox — distinct from the Agent cold-outreach engine. Returns status (active/draft), the sending mailbox, the ordered steps, and the connected mailboxes you can send from. One auto-provisioned sequence per account.

tools.name: update_follow_up
tools.description: Edit the warm follow-up sequence, choose the sending mailbox, or turn it on/off (write scope). steps = array of {subject, body, delay_days} (the first email needs a subject + body; use {{first_name}} to greet by name). mailbox_id = a connected mailbox to send from (list them via get_follow_up or get_mailbox). status = 'active' to turn on (needs a connected mailbox) or 'draft' to pause. Only ever emails leads you captured, never a bought list.

tools.name: redeem_promo_code
tools.description: Redeem a promo/discount code onto this account's Stripe customer; the discount applies from the next invoice. Returns the applied discount, or a clear error if the code is invalid/expired/already used or the account has no Stripe customer yet.

tools.name: find_buyers
tools.description: Preview the national buyer directory near a location. Buyer types: school, preschool (preschools & daycares), library, theater, fair, festival, parks (parks & recreation depts), museum, senior (senior-living/retirement communities), country_club, church, college (colleges & universities), live_music_venue (bars/restaurants that host live music), sports (pro NBA/WNBA + NCAA Division I teams). Returns total + counts by type + a small sample (no contact details). Give location (address or zip) OR lat & lng, a radius in miles, and optional types. Coverage for live_music_venue, preschool, parks, country_club, church and festival is still rolling out area-by-area, so a 0 count there just means that region isn't loaded yet. To actually receive verified contacts, place a lead order (order_leads), which spends lead credits.

tools.name: get_lead_credits
tools.description: This account's prepaid lead-credit balance and recent ledger (purchases, grants, delivery charges).

tools.name: list_lead_orders
tools.description: This account's buyer-lead orders and their status (pending/processing/done).

tools.name: get_lead_order
tools.description: One buyer-lead order with its progress (delivered/enriched counts).

tools.name: order_leads
tools.description: Place a buyer-lead order (MONEY scope — spends lead credits). Verified contacts are enriched asynchronously and enrolled into an outreach campaign (a new draft campaign is created unless campaign_id is given). Give location (address/zip) OR lat & lng, radius_mi, types (school, preschool, library, theater, fair, festival, parks, museum, senior, country_club, church, college, live_music_venue, sports), and target_count (capped to your current credit balance). Optional states (CSV of 2-letter codes, e.g. "MI") keeps delivery in-state when a wide radius would otherwise cross state lines. Each delivered lead is also saved to the tenant's permanent Contacts (deduped; tagged "Purchased leads"), so they own it for good — not just for the campaign. You're only charged for contacts actually delivered, so ordering more than exist in range is safe — run find_buyers first to see the available count.
